body.title: Send invoice throws TypeError in sendInvoice (InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48) and the send button does nothing
body.summary: The user opened a new invoice, filled in the customer and amount fields, clicked Save draft, then clicked Send invoice. The send click raised a TypeError reading 'id' of undefined, and the user then rage-clicked the Send invoice button without the invoice being sent.
body.expected: Clicking Send invoice sends the invoice without an error.
body.actual: Clicking Send invoice throws a TypeError (Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')) in sendInvoice at InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21, and the user rage-clicks the Send invoice button, which does not send the invoice.

evidence.note: The primary failure: uncaught TypeError in sendInvoice at InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21 when Send invoice is clicked.
The same TypeError is logged to the console, confirming the error occurs on the send action.
Five rapid clicks on #send-invoice show the user repeatedly tried to send and got no result.

body.suspected_cause: The sendInvoice handler likely reads an 'id' property from an object that is undefined at the time of the click (around InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48), possibly because the saved draft or customer data is not available to the send step.
body.signature: exc:TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') @ InvoiceSendButton.tsx

body.title: Send reminder fails with 500 (reported by [email])
body.summary: The user opened invoice inv_8812 and clicked Send reminder, which failed with a 500 from the reminders endpoint and showed a generic error. The user clicked Send reminder again a few seconds later and received the same 500 error.
body.expected: The reminder is sent and the user receives a success confirmation.
body.actual: POST /api/invoices/inv_8812/reminders returns 500 (internal_error) and the user sees "Something went wrong. Please try again." Retrying produces the same result.

evidence.note: Primary failure: reminders endpoint returns 500 with internal_error.
User-facing error message shown after the first failed send.
Same 500 on the retry, so the failure is repeatable.
Same generic error message shown on the retry.

body.suspected_cause: A likely server-side error in the reminders endpoint for this invoice is causing an unhandled exception, since the response is a consistent internal_error 500.

body.title: AR aging report times out with 504 after clicking AR aging on /reports
body.summary: The user opened /reports and clicked AR aging (#aging-report). The aging request to /api/reports/aging?range=… returned 504 gateway_timeout after 30012 ms, and the user saw a 'too long' message.
body.expected: The AR aging report loads and displays within the normal response time.
body.actual: The request to /api/reports/aging?range=… returns 504 (gateway_timeout) after 30012 ms, and the user sees 'This report is taking too long. Try a shorter range.' The user rage-clicks #aging-report while waiting.

evidence.note: The aging API request returns 504 gateway_timeout after 30012 ms, which is the primary failure.
The user rage-clicks #aging-report four times while the report is still loading, showing frustration with the wait.
The user is shown a timeout message suggesting a shorter range, so the report never displays.

body.suspected_cause: Likely the aging report query for the default range exceeds the gateway's 30-second timeout, so the request is cut off with a 504.

body.title: Payments page fails to load after deploy: chunk 812 returns 404
body.summary: The user opened the dashboard and clicked Payments, which led to /payments. The page did not load: the request for chunk 812 returned 404 and the user saw "Page failed to load."
body.actual: The request for GET /static/js/812.3f9a1c.chunk.js returns 404, a ChunkLoadError is thrown, and the user sees "Page failed to load."

evidence.note: Primary failure: the chunk request returns 404 in 35 ms.
The ChunkLoadError for chunk 812 is the exception the app throws from the missing chunk.
The user-facing error confirms the page did not load.

body.suspected_cause: Likely a stale-asset problem after the 2026.10.27-1 deploy: the page references chunk 812 from a build that is no longer served.

body.title: Customer CSV export fails with 500 and shows "Export failed." on /customers
body.summary: The user searched the customers page, typed into the card-number field, and clicked Export CSV. The export request to /api/customers/export returned a 500 after 920 ms, and the user saw "Export failed."

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the customers page (/customers with a search query).
Type into the card-number field (#card-number); the value is hidden in the recording.

body.expected: The customer CSV export completes and the file is produced without an error message.
body.actual: The export request returns HTTP 500 in 920 ms with the error code export_failed, and the UI shows "Export failed."

evidence.note: The export request to /api/customers/export returns 500 with export_failed, which is the primary failure.
The console logs an error for the failed export with a 500 status.
The user is shown the message "Export failed."

body.suspected_cause: The likely cause is a server-side error in the customers export endpoint, possibly triggered by the request's query parameters or by the card-number input, but the timeline does not confirm which.

body.title: QuickBooks 'Sync now' on /settings/integrations returns 500 sync_failed
body.summary: On the integrations settings page, the user clicked 'Sync now' for QuickBooks. The sync request failed with a 500 after about 5 seconds and the user was shown a 'Sync failed' message.
body.expected: The QuickBooks sync completes successfully without an error.
body.actual: The sync request POST /api/integrations/quickbooks/sync returned 500 in 5100 ms with sync_failed, and the user saw 'Sync failed. We'll retry automatically.'

evidence.note: The sync request returned a 500 error (sync_failed) after 5100 ms, which is the primary failure.
The user was shown a sync failure message, confirming the error reached the UI.

body.suspected_cause: The QuickBooks sync endpoint likely fails server-side (500 sync_failed) after a long delay of about 5 seconds, though the timeline does not show the underlying error.

body.title: Revenue report fails with RangeError when applying a custom date range
body.summary: The user opened the revenue report, opened the date range picker, typed a start date, and clicked Apply. The report then showed 'Something went wrong loading this report.' after an invalid time value error.
body.expected: The revenue report loads for the selected date range.
body.actual: The report fails to load and shows 'Something went wrong loading this report.' The console logs RangeError: Invalid time value at formatDateRange (DateRangePicker.tsx:112:9). The user then rage-clicked Apply six times.

evidence.note: Primary failure: uncaught RangeError in formatDateRange when applying the range.
User-visible error message shown on the report page.
Six rapid clicks on Apply suggest the user was stuck and retrying.

body.suspected_cause: The likely cause is that formatDateRange in DateRangePicker.tsx receives an unparseable date value from the date-from input and throws an invalid time value error instead of validating the input.

body.title: Payments page crashes with TypeError in formatRow when Refunds filter is clicked
body.summary: The user opened /payments and then clicked the Refunds filter (#filter-refunds). The app threw a TypeError reading 'amount' of null in formatRow and showed the message "Something went wrong." Same signature as BUG-280 (closed); likely a regression.
body.expected: The payments list filtered to refunds renders without error.
body.actual: A TypeError (Cannot read properties of null (reading 'amount') at formatRow, PaymentsTable.tsx:77:30) is thrown and the user sees "Something went wrong."

evidence.note: Uncaught TypeError in formatRow shows a row value is null when the refunds filter renders.
The user-facing error message appears at the same moment the exception is thrown.

body.suspected_cause: A likely cause is that formatRow in PaymentsTable.tsx reads .amount from a refund row that is null, with no null guard before the access.
body.signature: exc:TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'amount') @ PaymentsTable.tsx
